title: EZ: does a designed paradigm avoid the do/undo problem?
description:
Surfaced by the round-2 Codex review (2026-08-29), and it is the gap between what round 2 measured and what it wants to claim.

EZ's derivational lexicon holds CROSS-PARADIGM collisions at 0.00% — no slip turns a word into a member of a different stem's paradigm. That was verified independently. But the metric EXEMPTS paradigm-internal collisions on the grounds that they are 'a wrong form, not a wrong meaning', and the concepts in the experiment carry no semantics at all: paradigms are groups of adjacent frequency ranks, not meaning families.

Real morphology does not respect that exemption. 'do'/'undo', 'able'/'unable', 'possible'/'impossible' are morphological relatives whose confusion is a TRUTH-CONDITIONAL FLIP — the starboard/larboard configuration inside a paradigm. A derivational system that puts a negation affix one segment from the bare stem has built the worst possible pair by design.

QUESTION: can a paradigm be designed so that its internal confusions are all cheap? Concretely — affixes that are semantically 'safe' to confuse (tense, number, part of speech) may sit close; affixes that flip polarity, direction, or reference (negation, reversal, antonymy) must sit FAR from the stem and from each other. That is unequal error protection applied inside the word rather than across the lexicon, and it is testable as soon as the affix set carries meanings.

Until then, round 2's zero-damaging-error claim is scoped to 'no cross-paradigm hit' and must not be read as 'no damaging meaning errors' — the doc now says so.

comments.author: claude-conlang-ec
comments.text:
ROUND 3 BUILT (tools/ez_semantics.py), REVIEWED, REJECTED, REWRITTEN, and the finding came out STRONGER. Doc: docs/design/ez-error-corrected-lexicon.md 'Round 3'.

FIRST VERSION REJECTED (Codex xhigh, 2026-08-30), 2 blockers:
 (a) the damage classifier called EVERY tag mismatch damaging, including pairs that are not real contrasts (bare noun vs reversal-of-stem), and a two-segment 'floor' was then proved from an edge that does not exist;
 (b) the stem pool contained duplicates, so a 2004-word lexicon actually held 1992 forms from 249 stems while reporting 250.

REWRITTEN with a TYPED morphology: word = stem + PART-OF-SPEECH + POLARITY. POS markers are vowels (Esperanto shape); polarity is a suffix. POS mismatch = CHEAP (syntax expected one category, got another). Polarity mismatch = DAMAGING. Worst case = SAME-SLOT: same stem, same POS, opposite polarity — literally do/undo.

RESULT (2004 words, 334 paradigms, 0 illegal, 0 duplicates, 0 cross-stem collisions):
  naive, 1-segment negator   damaging 2.81% | same-slot 2.81% | cheap 8.79% | 2-err 6.5% | 4.46 seg
  hazard-aware, 2-segment    damaging 0.00% | same-slot 0.00% | cheap 8.51% | 2-err 5.7% | 4.92 seg

EVERY negated word in the naive design is one slip from its own positive: 1002 pairs of 1002. Not most — all.

THE CENTRAL FINDING, which the review's criticism produced: sweeping all nine attested one-segment negators gives an IDENTICAL 2.81% and IDENTICAL 1002 same-slot pairs. The damage does not come from picking a confusable segment; it comes from the INSERTION EDGE — stemPOS and stemPOS+N differ by exactly one insertion for ANY segment N. Choosing a 'distinctive' negation marker buys literally nothing.

THE DESIGN LAW: a one-segment polarity marker is unsafe in every language that has one. Not confusable-segment-dependent, not phonology-dependent — a consequence of adding one segment being one error. Fix costs 10.3% more segments and drives damage to zero (and improves two-error 6.5% -> 5.7%).

GENERALIZES: RZ has the same disease one level up — 'no' one slip from 'lo'. Whether polarity rides on an affix or a particle, the cheapest form in the language carries the most expensive distinction, because brevity is allocated by frequency and negation is frequent. The standard lexicon rule misses it because it screens UNRELATED minimal pairs and these are related.

Re-review of the corrected version is running.

comments.author: claude-conlang-ec
comments.text:
RE-REVIEWED (Codex xhigh). The core result was VERIFIED SOUND: all ten one-segment negators identical at full precision (2.8108011716%, 1002 pairs); 1002 = 334x3 forced by construction, not by selective packing; naive and protected designs select the SAME 334 stems in the same order, so the length cost is not stem-selection confounding; integrity clean at defaults.

TWO BLOCKERS REMAINED, both now fixed:

(1) 'unsafe in every language' overreached. The proof covers a strictly CONCATENATIVE polarity opposition under an insertion/deletion channel. It says nothing about replacement exponents, stem alternation, or redundant agreement. Narrowed to: every strictly concatenative one-segment polarity opposition contains a distance-one same-slot pair.

(2) integrity() reported counts but ASSERTED nothing; '--minlen 100' printed an empty table and exited 0. Now raises IntegrityError on illegal forms, duplicates, shortfall, cross-stem collisions, or partial paradigms; an empty run is fatal; non-multiples of the paradigm size print a rounding note. Verified: --minlen 100 now exits 1.

THE NARROWING PRODUCED A BETTER DESIGN. If polarity and part of speech fuse into one PORTMANTEAU marker (-po noun vs -ko negated noun), negation becomes a SUBSTITUTION rather than an insertion — and unlike an insertion, a substitution can be made non-confusable by choosing distant consonants. Measured, it wins nearly everything:
  naive 1-segment      damaging 2.81% | cheap 9.01% | 2-err 6.4% | 2.00 syl | 4.46 seg
  hazard-aware 2-seg   damaging 0.00% | cheap 8.72% | 2-err 5.7% | 2.46 syl | 4.92 seg
  replacement portm.   damaging 0.00% | cheap 7.96% | 2-err 4.8% | 2.00 syl | 5.00 seg
Best damaging, cheap and tail rates, and the SAME syllable count as naive, because negatives stop being longer than positives. Costs segments (5.00 vs 4.46) — so which fix is cheaper depends on syllables vs segments, the same unresolved ambiguity as round 1.

ALSO ADDED, per the review: the C (/ts/) coda was missing from the 'every attested' sweep (now ten, result unchanged); 'choosing a distinctive marker buys nothing at all' narrowed to the same-slot floor only, since the cheap rate does vary 8.5-9.6%; 'as extra length always does' removed (the replacement design is longer AND better in the tail, which contradicts it); evidence markers added to the Zipf/negation-frequency premises.

MOST IMPORTANT ADDITION — the typing assumption is doing most of the work, and it is now shown. Scoring part-of-speech mismatches as cheap assumes syntax catches them. With syntax catching fraction q, effective damaging = damaging + (1-q) x cheap:
        q=1.0   q=0.9   q=0.5   q=0.0
naive   2.81%   3.71%   7.32%  11.82%
hazard  0.00%   0.87%   4.36%   8.72%
replace 0.00%   0.80%   3.98%   7.96%
ANY q<1 removes the zero. What survives at every q is the ordering and a ~3-point gap. The 'zero' belongs to q=1 and must never be quoted without it. q is unmeasured [H].

title: Set the evidence bar EZ must clear before any 'dominates' claim is publishable
description:
Codex review closed with this offer and it is worth taking: define the minimum experimental standard before another comparative claim goes in the paper. Round 1 made three claims that did not survive review, all for the same underlying reason — the instrument's assumptions were not swept before the conclusion was written.

The standard, as a checklist for any future EZ-vs-anything claim:
1. LENGTH must be reported in BOTH syllables and segments, and no brevity claim may be made without a duration model. (EZ min-6 is shorter in syllables and 38% longer in segments — the syllable-only figure was the blocker.)
2. Any conclusion depending on the error mix must be SWEPT across it, not stated at the default. The two-error ordering between EZ and RZ inverts between a 60/30/10 and a 95/2.5/2.5 mix.
3. Any lexicon optimized against the confusion graph must ALSO be scored off-model, since RZ is not fitted to it and EZ is. The e~o / i~u sweep is the current minimum.
4. Design dials that were held fixed must be swept before being described as findings — the syllable-palette cap turned out to change robustness at fixed length, which falsified 'length is the only fix'.
5. Causal claims ('because the sound space is roomy') require the experiment that isolates the cause, or they are stated as correlations.
6. Frequency weighting must be identical on both sides or the difference must be stated.

tools/ez_sensitivity.py implements 1-4 and should be run before, not after, the write-up.

comments.author: claude-conlang-ec
comments.text:
STRENGTHENED after the round-2 review, which found two more blockers of the same species — the instrument was not checked against its own stated rules before conclusions were written. Add to the checklist:

7. INTEGRITY ASSERTIONS ARE NOT OPTIONAL. Every generated lexicon must assert, in code, that every word satisfies every rule the experiment claims to enforce: phonotactically legal, harmony-compatible if harmony is on, distance rule respected against everything outside its paradigm. Round 2's first version had 1000 of 2000 words failing legality and nobody noticed because nothing checked. tools/ez_structure.py now reports illegal_forms / nonharmonic_forms / shortfall on every row and they must all read zero.

8. NO SILENT SHORTFALL. If the pool cannot supply the requested concepts, report the gap; never renormalise weights over the survivors and compare against full-size rows.

9. ANY 'BITS' OR INFORMATION MEASURE MUST BE INVARIANT TO THE ENUMERATION. Test it: hold the output lexicon fixed and enlarge the unused candidate pool. If the number moves, the measure is reporting the pool, not the lexicon.

10. A METRIC THAT EXEMPTS A CLASS OF ERRORS MUST SAY WHAT THE CLASS MEANS. 'Zero cross-paradigm collisions' sounds like 'zero damaging errors' and is not, when the paradigms carry no semantics.

comments.author: claude-conlang-ez
comments.text:
ITEM 11, added after the round-5 review (2026-08-30) — the most expensive one so far.

11. ANY GREEDY PASS OVER AN ORDERED CANDIDATE POOL MUST RANDOMISE THE ARBITRARY PART OF THAT ORDER AND REPORT THE SPREAD. Round 5 found this failure twice in one round, in two different tools, and in both cases the fixed order was silently deciding the answer:
  - ez_mint.mint() walked its pool shortest-and-simplest-first. Shuffling within length classes improved off-model robustness 17-95x and the two-error tail 12-25x at identical word length, and retired round 1's central finding (conlang-4d8).
  - ez_frontier's repair search took the alphabetically first safe candidate. 'C', 'J', 'L', 'N' sort before every lowercase phoneme, so every repair prefixed one of the four rarest consonants in the inventory.

Test for it the way item 9 tests bits-invariance: hold everything fixed, permute the arbitrary order, and re-measure. If the headline moves, the headline was a property of the enumeration.

12. PRINT THE ARTIFACT, NOT ONLY THE AGGREGATE. Both tie-break bugs and the syllabify bug (conlang-w2e) were invisible in every summary table and obvious in the first twelve concrete rows. Any generative experiment must render a sample of what it actually produced before its aggregates are believed.

title: Score RZ on description length so the EZ head-to-head is fair
description:
docs/design/ez-error-corrected-lexicon.md Round 2 measures EZ variants against each other on description length (bits a learner must store). RZ is entered as '~0 for a zone reader', which is an honest statement about cognates but NOT a measured quantity on the same scale — so the head-to-head is currently incomplete in RZ's favour on that column.

To close it: RZ has regular derivation (rz-grammar §9) and tools/coverage.py already separates surface coverage from lemma coverage (the 'regularity dividend'). What is missing is a morphological analysis of the RZ lexicon good enough to count how many arbitrary STEMS a learner must store vs how many forms fall out of the rules — the same split ez_structure.py computes for EZ.

Then the comparison becomes: EZ needs 250-1000 arbitrary stems that resemble nothing; RZ needs N arbitrary stems, most of which a Romance reader already knows. The difference is the real admission price of the engineered approach, and it is currently the only thing standing between EZ and being the better design on every measured axis.

title: GZ root policy: make clipping TRUNCATION-ONLY, so the colloquial form is a prefix of the citation form
description:
Falls out of the Codex review of the progressive-redundancy doc (2026-08-28), and it is the cheapest item on that page.

The R3 citation register is only MONOTONE — i.e. only a redundancy rung rather than a second vocabulary — if the colloquial form is a PREFIX of the citation form. Then the citation register EXTENDS the signal instead of REPLACING it, and an R0 listener can stop at the clip boundary and still be correct.

GZ's current root policy ('adapt the Romance form when it fits the scheme cheaply, coin or clip when it doesn't' — gz-sketch.md) permits both truncation (fenestra -> fenes) and substitution (fenestra -> fesa). Substitutive clipping breaks monotonicity and turns the citation register into a diglossia.

PROPOSAL: make truncation binding in the root policy. Costs nothing — it constrains a policy that has not been exercised at scale yet — and it is a precondition for the whole citation-register story being coherent. Adopt independently of any decision about the expensive R2 dispersion pass.

Doc: docs/design/gz-progressive-redundancy.md §8.

title: E/R/M bake-off needs an error-correction column: concord-as-parity vs the E-scheme final rime
description:
The z0s E/R/M bake-off (GZ-internal since the mining audit) has never priced the schemes on error correction. It should, because E and concord COMPETE FOR THE SAME PHYSICAL CHANNEL.

The E-scheme spends the final rime on POS (-o noun, -a adj, -e adv). Romance concord lives in exactly that rime. So adopting E does not merely fail to buy concord — it forecloses it, by spending the slot concord would use. That is a real cost the bake-off currently does not see.

Esperanto is the precedent that says the competition is RESOLVABLE at the cost of a second slot: -o/-a for POS, then -j/-n stacked after it for number/case. Ido dropped adjective agreement entirely and is the other data point.

Connects to: the R4 rung of the redundancy ladder (concord-as-parity is what R4 buys back after D3 sold it) and to conlang-ymu item 6.

title: Coinage screen: add the same-slot (starboard/larboard) rule and the tolerance-band audit
description:
gz-rz-mining-audit.md verdict 6 bought the coinage-screen POLICY with the instrument pending. Two criteria to add before the instrument is built (docs/design/gz-progressive-redundancy.md §5, §3):

1. SAME-SLOT RULE (starboard/larboard, from the 2026-08-25 chat): never license antonyms or same-slot contrasts as form-neighbours; neighbours may share a semantic field only if confusing them is cheap or context disambiguates. NOTE THE STRUCTURAL PROBLEM: a closed class is BY CONSTRUCTION a set of same-slot contrasts, so any two function words that land near each other in form space are automatically in the worst configuration. The rule and the closed-class inventory are on a collision course by definition — the screen has to run over function words, which it never has.

2. TOLERANCE-BAND AUDIT: rz-spoken-standard.md §4 absorbs a band of accented realizations (soft-c~s, v~b) as legitimate RZ. That band is a set of DECLARED phoneme mergers, and a pair distinguished only by a band-internal contrast is homophonous for those listeners permanently, by spec, with no noise required. Measured today: ZERO collisions — a clean bill, but the first time it has been checked. Must re-run on every lexicon growth pass.

Also on record from the same measurement: three groups are ALREADY homophones in the prescribed broadcast realization — 'a'~'ha' (preposition vs perfect auxiliary), 'hora'~'ora', 'casa'~'cassa'. Silent h did that.

Instrument: tools/gz_redundancy.py implements both checks; fold them into the coinage screen tool when it is built.

title: Reconcile error ABSORPTION with distributed parity: they are the same dial read backwards
description:
docs/design/gz-progressive-redundancy.md §6. Absorption declarations D1-D7 (rz-error-absorption.md, normative rz-grammar §10) WIDEN the set of legal forms; parity NARROWS it. They are the same dial in opposite directions and no doc in the repo had noticed. rz-spoken-standard.md §4 does the same thing on the phonetic axis and says so explicitly ('mirroring error-absorption on the phonetic axis').

CRITERION SWAP PROPOSED: the adopted licence for absorption is 'an error that changes no truth conditions and blocks no parse should be defined as variation' — a fact about the ERROR. The right criterion is a fact about the CONSTRAINT GRAPH: absorb only where the information the constraint carried is recoverable from ANOTHER constraint. Local over-determination is the licence; truth-conditional harmlessness is necessary, not sufficient.

RE-AUDIT RESULT: D2, D4, D5, D6, D7 survive untouched. D1 and D3 do not — and they are exactly the two that touch CROSS-WORD redundancy, the class the error-correction chat identifies as natural language's graceful-degradation layer (harmony, templates, concord as distributed parity). RZ deleted gender, so D3 turned off the last concord channel it had. The project sold its LDPC layer for learner hours without knowing that was what it was selling.

NOT a proposal to reverse D1/D3 — absorption is worth its price on the production side. The proposal is that the relaxation belongs on a RUNG: off in low registers, on in high ones. Absorption and parity stop competing the moment they are on the same ladder.

Deliverable: the criterion written into rz-error-absorption.md as the standing test for future declarations, + the D1/D3 rung scoping.

comments.author: claude-conlang-ec
comments.text:
SHARPENED after Codex review (2026-08-28). The original framing had one criterion; it needs two, because the review showed the single criterion conflates them:
  (a) CONTENT RECOVERABILITY — is the meaning the constraint carried recoverable elsewhere?
  (b) CHECK PRESERVATION — is the detection event it produced still produced?
Absorption is licensed by (a); what it COSTS is (b), and (b) has never been on the ledger.

Re-audit under both axes (this replaces the earlier D1/D3 verdicts):
  D1 — KEEP UNCHANGED. The earlier verdict misread its scope (see the polarity bead). Content recoverable (nada carries polarity) AND check preserved (nada is still an audible negative element). D1 is simply safe.
  D2 — keep, but relabel honestly: definiteness is NOT recoverable, so D2 is an information loss accepted on truth-conditional grounds, not a free relaxation.
  D3 — THE REAL FINDING, and the only one. Adjective number is semantically recoverable from the noun and determiner, so it passes the adopted criterion; but it is the only cross-word parity RZ still had, and agreement is the one check that catches a VALID-WORD -> VALID-WORD corruption, which no word-internal check can see. Semantically free, detection-expensive: exactly the case the adopted criterion cannot see.
  D4-D7 — keep, both axes clean.

So the deliverable narrows: write the TWO-AXIS test into rz-error-absorption.md as the standing test for future declarations, and scope D3's relaxation to a rung (off in low registers, on in high).

comments.author: claude-conlang-ec
comments.text:
ROUND 4 CLOSES THE LOOP ON D1, and it is a stronger argument than §6 made.

Round 4 (tools/ez_sentence.py) measured how much syntax catches: 84-100% of part-of-speech errors, and EXACTLY 0% of polarity errors. A negated verb is still a verb, so no category-checking slot can ever reject it.

The Codex review then supplied the correction that matters here: it is not that NO syntax can catch a polarity error — it is that CATEGORY-CHECKING syntax cannot. A grammar with obligatory NEGATIVE CONCORD does catch it, because a lost negator leaves its agreement partner stranded.

Which means D1 is exactly the thing that gives that check away. RZ's D1 makes negative concord OPTIONAL. Under the two-axis test this bead proposes, D1 passes on axis (a) — content recoverable, 'nada' still carries the polarity — and that is why the earlier audit marked it KEEP. But axis (b) is where it bites: making concord optional removes the only syntactic check that can see a polarity error at all. D1 is not unsafe for the clauses it governs; it is unsafe as a POLICY, because it forecloses the one grammatical mechanism that covers the clauses it does not govern.

So the D1 verdict moves from 'keep, unchanged' to 'keep the permission, but do not let it become the norm': negative concord should be the REQUIRED form in the high registers of the ladder (gz-progressive-redundancy.md R4), precisely so that polarity has a cross-word check when the channel is bad. That is the same rung-scoping conclusion this bead already reaches for D3, now with a measured reason rather than an analogy.

Cross-refs: the polarity bead (conlang-1op) and the round-3/4 sections of docs/design/ez-error-corrected-lexicon.md.

title: R3 citation register for GZ: reprice — the high-redundancy register IS the zonal-fidelity register
description:
The ymu routing packet flagged citation-vs-colloquial register (rateless coding by register shift) as a new user-visible capability needing an Edward gate. gz-progressive-redundancy.md §8 changes its price: GZ's root policy already clips donor forms, so the UNCLIPPED donor form is the citation form for free — and it is MORE zonally transparent than the colloquial form, not less. The high-redundancy register and the high-fidelity/bootstrap register are the same object. That makes R3 ~0 cost and plausibly negative (it is also the listening on-ramp and the safety register).

Deliverable: decision packet for Edward with the repriced number, plus the 'V as in Victor with the donor language as the phonetic alphabet' framing.

title: GZ progressive redundancy ladder: define the dated default + its evidence gate
description:
gz-progressive-redundancy.md §8 proposes six rungs (R0 dense colloquial / R1 phonotactic floor / R2 dispersed closed class / R3 citation register / R4 concord-on + absorption-off / R5 frames+checksum+readback) and the actual novelty: the spec ships a DATED DEFAULT — GZ defaults to R3-R4 while the community is young, with a precommitted schedule for dropping the default toward R0-R1 as priors accumulate. The migration is a policy change about which rung is unmarked, not a change to the language, so no re-standardization and no diglossia.

WHAT THIS BEAD OWES: (1) the evidence gate — what measurement licenses dropping the default rung, and who decides; (2) the monotonicity proof obligation per rung (a rung-N-1 reader must parse rung-N text); (3) the self-labeling check (each rung's mechanism is its own marker, so no negotiation particle).

Precedent claim to verify: no engineered language plans its own densification; natural languages densify by erosion and cannot steer it.

title: Re-derive every flagged RZ lexical/grammatical decision under the chosen objective
description:
Once ym3.2 settles the objective and the §1 weights follow from it, every decision currently flagged "cloze will tell" or "currently the former" becomes derivable rather than taste. Sweep them all in one pass so the lexicon is internally consistent with one stated rule.

## Known flagged items

**romance-zonal-v0.md §9 (open questions):**
- `voler`/`poter` (IT/FR, current pick) vs `querer`/`poder` (Ibero .65-.82). Population weighting flips this to querer/poder decisively.
- `alora` (Italo-French .30, "prettier") vs `entonce` (Ibero majority). The recipe weights already say entonce; only taste is holding alora.
- `fenestra` vs `ventana`. ES plurality alone under population weighting; fenestra holds IT+FR+RO plus the derivation family plus a weak English hook (defenestrate, fenestration).
- `soplar` — flagged weak for IT/FR readers.
- `les` vs invariant `le`.
- Reference pronunciation for c/g before e,i (/ts/ vs /tS/ vs /s/).
- Subjunctive: none in v0.

**rz-grammar.md flags:**
- §3 `on`-impersonal vs `se`-impersonal (Ibero readers may prefer se).
- §4 perfect-of-result `tener` + participle vs `haber` (flagged as possibly odd to IT/FR).
- §4.1 `es`/`sta` split — Ibero-right, marked for IT/FR where essere/etre covers both.
- §7 `aunque` (Ibero-heavy; IT benche, FR bien que lose).
- §8 higher ordinals (deliberate escape hatch).
- §11 weekdays `lunedi/martedi` (IT forms, chosen for family regularity) vs Ibero `lunes/martes`.

## Two structural fixes to apply in the same pass

1. **Collapse ES+PT into one bloc where they agree.** Highest-value change and independent of which objective wins. ES and PT agree on most contested items, so counting them separately aggregates three-ish opinions while appearing to aggregate five. Interlingua's control-group rule is the precedent; RZ currently lacks it.
2. **Reconcile §4's tie-break ladder with §1's weights.** §4 is a lexicographic ordering (sight-recognition -> derivation regularity -> English cognate -> shorter), §1 is a weighted sum. Same decisions, two aggregation rules, never squared. Pick one and express the other in its terms.

## Watch item

Under population weighting the whole set resolves Ibero and RZ becomes "regularized Spanish" — which incidentally resolves conlang-wan toward FORK, since it is the single change that most differentiates RZ from Interlingua. Do not treat that as a free win: it trades the neutrality asset for the reach asset, and §6/§7 of romance-zonal-v0.md assume neutrality in the bootstrap story.

Also flag any item where the chosen objective and the false-friend screen (§4.5) disagree; the screen is mandatory and overrides.

title: Verify the Romance reader-base figures against primary sources
description:
Every population number in the weighting analysis (conlang-8zy, conlang-ym3) is from an agent's memory, not a source. Nothing should depend on them until checked.

Approximate figures currently in play, to verify:
- Spanish ~485M L1 (~600M with L2) — cross-check Instituto Cervantes annual report
- Portuguese ~235M L1
- French ~74-80M L1, ~310-320M total — OIF claims are promotional, treat with care; the L1/L2 gap matters more for FR than any other source
- Italian ~65M L1
- Romanian ~24-25M L1

Decisions this feeds, all of which are sensitive at the 5-10 point level:
1. **L1 vs L2 vs literate-reader base.** RZ is written-FIRST, so the relevant denominator is READERS, not speakers. French is the sharp case: its huge L2 base is concentrated in West/Central Africa with varying literacy-in-French rates, while its written cognates are unusually valuable because French orthography stayed Latin even where its phonology left (romance-zonal-v0.md §1 already notes this). Population-by-speakers and population-by-readers give materially different French weights.
2. Whether Spanish L2 (~100M) counts. Pure "speaker population" is ambiguous exactly where it changes the answer.
3. Whether to use a current snapshot at all — ES/PT growth is in the Americas and Africa, IT/RO populations are shrinking. A weighting frozen to 2026 ages.

Deliverable: a sourced table in romance-zonal-v0.md §1 (or a companion data file) with an explicit statement of which denominator is being used and why. No design decisions here — this is the fact base the design decision sits on.

title: Spatial layer: implement UNLWS 'hashing' for distant coreference (a miniature of the referent, not a lane)
description: From the UNLWS review (docs/design/unlws-review.md, 2026-08-27). Sai lists three ways to refer at a distance: pronouns (a closed symbol set), POINTING (an arrow toward the target), and HASHING — 'a hash pronoun would look like its target, but a somehow simplified version'. Hashing is the most valuable single steal from UNLWS because it directly attacks the cost we measured. A referent lane costs O(distance): the line must physically span the page, which is why lanes measured 3.15x prose in the character test and 4.5x in area, and why lane pitch caps the page at 9-16 referents. A hash pronoun costs O(1) local ink wherever it appears, and unlike an ordinary pronoun it is SELF-IDENTIFYING — you can see which referent it is without tracking a line or resolving an antecedent. Concretely for us: render a distant mention as a reduced form of the entity's own glyph (in the current English prototype, the first 1-2 characters plus the entity tint; in GZ, a reduced script block). Then measure the same diagnostics against S1 lanes: search area per referent, marks per proposition, and ink area. Hypothesis worth falsifying: hashing keeps most of the reference-tracking win at a fraction of the area, which would make the lane mechanism unnecessary. Note this also interacts with conlang-p6f (grammatical coreference marking) — if the grammar marked coreference, hashing would be its natural rendering.

title: GZ: should the grammar mark coreference (switch-reference or obviation)?
description: Raised 2026-08-27 by the spatial-layer work. Coreference is the one thing no grammar in the comparison helps with (English pronouns ambiguous; Chinese drops arguments entirely; GZ inherits ordinary Romance pronouns) — and it is exactly what the referent-lane layout was invented to fix, which means the layout is doing work the language could do itself. Two attested mechanisms would supply it grammatically: SWITCH-REFERENCE (widespread in Papuan and North American families) marks on each clause whether the NEXT clause's subject is the same referent or a different one — one bit per clause, and coreference becomes a grammatical fact rather than an inference; OBVIATION (Algonquian) makes one third person proximate and the other obviative, with the marking persisting across clauses, so 'he' and 'the other he' are formally distinct. Either would hand a spatial renderer its lanes for free, and both are cheap enough to teach. Costs: one more obligatory channel on every clause (switch-reference) or a tracked discourse status per referent (obviation), plus interaction with the POS/TAM channels already spoken for. Also note the prototype currently gets coreference FREE AND FAKE — test texts repeat the identical lexeme, so string matching suffices; real text uses pronouns and definite descriptions. HUMAN GATE: changes what the language is.

title: GZ: should roots declare PLACE STRUCTURE (Lojban-style), not just POS-alternation class?
description: Raised by the spatial-layer grammar-fit analysis (docs/design/spatial-layer-grammar-fit.md, 2026-08-27). GZ already declares a POS-alternation class per root (O/A/P/R), which tells you how the root behaves under noun/verb/modifier alternation but NOT how many arguments it takes. Lojban declares full place structure per predicate (x1..x5, each with a fixed meaning), and UNLWS independently reaches the same design via glyph attachment points — two systems converging is a signal. For the spatial layer this is the single cheapest grammar change that would materially help: the renderer could allocate the right frame per clause (two slots for an intransitive, three for a transitive) instead of forcing a fixed agent/pred/patient/misc grid that leaves holes, which is exactly the awkwardness Edward flagged on 'stone come from mountain'. Cost side: one more declared fact per root, the same price the alternation class already charges, and it constrains the lexicon. HUMAN GATE: this changes what the language IS, not just how it renders, so it is Edward's call, not the rendering lane's.
design:
EXPANDED 2026-08-27 after reviewing UNLWS.

THE PROPOSAL. Today a GZ root declares a POS-alternation class (O/A/P/R) — how it behaves under noun/verb/modifier alternation. It does NOT declare how many arguments it takes or what they mean. The proposal is to add that: each root declares an ordered place structure, Lojban-style, where each place has a fixed semantic role.

  build:  x1 the builder, x2 the thing built, x3 the material, x4 the site
  come:   x1 the mover, x2 the source, x3 the goal
  hold:   x1 the thing holding, x2 the load

WHY IT KEEPS COMING UP. Three independent lines of work converged on it this week:
 (a) The renderer needs it. Every layout currently forces a fixed agent/predicate/patient/misc frame onto every clause, so an intransitive leaves an empty patient cell — which is exactly the awkwardness Edward flagged on 'stone come from mountain'. With declared places the renderer allocates the right frame per clause: two slots for an intransitive, four for build.
 (b) UNLWS reached the same design from the graphics side. Its glyphs carry ATTACHMENT POINTS 'symbolically related to their roles', and Sai draws the consequence explicitly: 'Changes in role requirements would be visually represented as a simple presence or absence of those attachment-points.' Valency is drawn rather than implied — an intransitive glyph simply has no patient attachment point, so there is no empty slot because there was never a slot.
 (c) It subsumes the oblique problem. Places absorb what are currently particle-marked obliques (come-from becomes x2, not a de-phrase), which shrinks the grab-bag misc column that Edward made me collapse in S4.

WHAT IT COSTS THE LEARNER. One more declared fact per root — the same kind of price the alternation class already charges, and payable the same way (it is in the dictionary entry, not in a paradigm to memorize). The real costs are elsewhere: (1) place ORDER must be memorized per root, which is Lojban's most-complained-about feature and its biggest learnability tax; (2) it constrains lexicon design, since every new root needs its places designed, not just its meaning; (3) it interacts with the particle class — if places cover the common roles, several of the 26 clitics lose most of their work.

THE MITIGATION WORTH TESTING. Lojban's tax is that place ORDER is arbitrary and must be recalled. QA-SRL (He, Lewis and Zettlemoyer, EMNLP 2015) shows the fix: replace role CODES with natural-language QUESTIONS ('who built something?', 'what was it built from?'). Non-experts reached P.81/R.86 after under two hours, against 30-40 hours for a code-based scheme, because the question IS the label and there is nothing to memorize. If GZ places are named by question words rather than by number, the memorization tax may largely vanish. That combination — declared places, question-named — is the actual proposal and it is not something Lojban tried.

DECISION SHAPE. Adopting this changes what the language IS, not how it renders, so it is Edward's call. The cheap first step, if he wants evidence before deciding: declare places for the ~30 roots in the seed lexicon only, render the spatial layouts from them, and see whether the frames-with-holes problem actually disappears and how much the misc column shrinks. That is reversible and costs no commitment.

The closest (Rasamimanana et al. 2025, Cognitive Science 49(7):e70081, N=40) has the comic carrying only 33-37% of the source word count, ~43% comprehension in BOTH formats, and per-fixation processing 25% SLOWER in comics — a navigation win, not a comprehension-rate win. title: Spatial layer: metrics should come from semantic mark records, not SVG reparsing
description: Codex xhigh code review 2026-08-26, remaining findings after the 3 blockers were fixed in 686774e. (a) BLOCKER-level: count_crossings only sees <line> elements, so ring arcs and polygon edges are invisible while negation strikes and tense rules are counted as edges; count_marks counts a box+label as two marks, a polygon as one, a <path> as zero. These are SVG-serialization artifacts, not comparable structural metrics. Fix: layouts should return explicit semantic mark and connector records, and metrics compute from those. (b) S3's share statistic has mismatched units - total_shares counts repeated arguments while satisfied increments at most once per clause, so multi-share clauses are undercounted; ent_slot only considers the first canonical occurrence. (c) S3 permits real overlap: collision begins below 2R-4 rather than 2R, and the shared-entity early continue drops modifiers on a shared mention. (d) S1 records geometry it does not draw: modifier diamonds are drawn at yy but recorded at yy+12; gutter extents are approximate. This directly corrupts scatter and search. (e) serial_binding_span reconstructs positions in argument order rather than retaining source token offsets, so it does not measure what it claims. (f) tests compare mention SETS not occurrence counts, predicate checks are substring checks, and the canvas test ignores the enclosing <g transform>. (g) rasterize.render ignores Chrome's return code and only checks that the path exists, so a failed render can silently reuse a stale PNG; it also parses only the first 600 bytes for width/height. (h) dead code: _clusters, Layout.crossings, metrics(...,ents) parameter, S5 pred_pos, Clause.tokens accounting.

title: Spec gaps the redundancy instrument hit: geminates and gu before front vowels
description:
Surfaced by the Codex review of tools/gz_redundancy.py (2026-08-28). Neither is a bug in the tool; both are places where rz-spoken-standard.md §4 does not say enough for an instrument to follow it.

1. GEMINATES. §4 prescribes 'every letter audible (except the one declared silent h)', and RZ declares no length contrast. So <ss>, <nn>, <rr> in inherited spellings (cassa, anno, guerra) have no stated realization. The tool originally collapsed them, which MANUFACTURED a casa~cassa homophone that no rule licenses; it now keeps them, which is the conservative choice for a detection measure. Either answer is defensible — the spec should pick one.

2. GU BEFORE FRONT VOWELS. The tool reads <gue>/<gui> as /ge/,/gi/ (guerra = /gerra/), which is the Ibero/Italian convention RZ's spellings clearly assume — sangue, guerra — but §4 does not state it. Same for <qu>, which the tool reads as /k/ before front vowels and /kw/ elsewhere.

Both are one-line additions to the spoken standard. Until they land, tools/gz_redundancy.py documents its choices inline and flags them [D — specification gap].

title: Trailhead (cheap, parked): route content by dependency — the GPU half of the CPU idea
description:
Edward 2026-08-27, second half of the same thought: 'or we might do some GPU thing for some movie-like media.' Parked as a trailhead, not active work.

The residue worth keeping: a GPU is throughput-oriented and wins on work that is embarrassingly parallel — no dependencies between items. A CPU wins on dependent chains. Applied to discourse, that suggests ROUTING BY DEPENDENCY rather than choosing one format for a whole text: the parts of a text whose elements are mutually independent (a cast of characters, a set of simultaneous states, a scene, a taxonomy's siblings, an inventory) go to the wide parallel channel — a spatial or pictorial rendering; the parts that form a dependency chain (narrative sequence, an argument, a proof, a procedure) stay in the serial channel, where reordering (conlang-<cpu bead>) is the lever instead.

That reframes the whole spatial-layer question from 'which format wins' to 'which SPANS of a text belong in which channel', and it is computable from the same dependency graph the scheduler would build. It also connects to Edward's earlier 'a picture is worth a thousand words' thread and to the movie/comics prior art (Rasamimanana et al.: comics were a navigation win, not a comprehension-rate win, and panel viewing time tracked the TEXT in the speech bubbles — i.e. the propositional load rode the serial channel even inside the parallel medium).

title: Spatial layer: typed connection lines (UNLWS's six copulas + conceptual set)
description: From the UNLWS review, 2026-08-27. Every layout we have built uses exactly ONE line type — a bar or connector that means 'these are related'. UNLWS types the line and gets a great deal of expressiveness for free: six COPULAR types (equation, attribution/description, proper inclusion/subset, locational, possessive, existential) distinguished by 'different squiggles on the line'; a CONCEPTUAL set (causation, theory/data support, argument structure, source attribution, emotional/experiential association, generic association); and META-modifications layered on top (metaphoricity marking, and evidentiality: perceived / reported / tautological / habitual). Line style is a channel we are simply not using and it costs no extra glyphs, no extra area, and no extra marks by the count_marks metric. Relevant to the project beyond the spatial layer: evidentials are already Tier 3 on the design brief, and this would render them without adding spoken morphology. Caution from the same review: this adds expressiveness, and Stenning and Oberlander's result is that graphical processibility comes FROM limited abstraction — so each added line type should be justified against a task, not added because it is cheap.

title: env: cmux claude-hook errors in daemonized bg sessions (Failed to write to socket)
description:
Every background Claude session dispatched from cmux emits a visible 'UserPromptSubmit hook error / Failed with non-blocking status code: Error: Failed to write to socket' banner.

ROOT CAUSE (diagnosed 2026-08-25, session 77538ad4):
cmux injects 6 hooks via --settings at dispatch (SessionStart/Stop/SessionEnd/Notification/UserPromptSubmit/PreToolUse -> 'cmux claude-hook <x>'). Claude Code's bg-job daemon persists those in respawnFlags and re-applies them. But the bg session runs under 'claude bg-pty-host' whose PPID is 1 (daemonized) -- the cmux app (pid 1411) is NOT an ancestor.

cmux's control socket (~/Library/Application Support/cmux/cmux.sock) enforces a peer check. Direct probe: connect() succeeds, send() succeeds, and the server replies:
  'ERROR: Access denied — only processes started inside cmux can connect'
The cmux CLI mislabels that response as 'Failed to write to socket' and exits 1, which Claude Code surfaces as a hook error.

NOT env-based: all CMUX_* vars (CMUX_SOCKET_PATH, CMUX_SURFACE_ID, CMUX_WORKSPACE_ID...) are present and inherited, and it is still denied -- so the discriminator is process ancestry/audit session, which daemonization severs.

IMPACT: cosmetic + ~0.3s per prompt submit. Non-blocking. Confirmed present since session launch: 1037 occurrences in the transcript, first at 2026-08-21T16:15:10 (~2 min after the 16:13:00 launch). NOT a recent regression -- the 'socket rebound at 21:49 today' hypothesis was tested and refuted.

NO LEAK: hook procs are transient (~0.29s); an apparent '7 lingering procs' was a pgrep false positive matching the hook JSON inside other claude processes' --settings blob.

UPSTREAM FIX (manaflow-ai/cmux): (1) 'cmux claude-hook' should exit 0 when it cannot reach the app -- it is a best-effort UI status ping, not a gate; (2) report 'access denied' rather than 'Failed to write to socket'; (3) authorize via an inherited env token instead of process ancestry, since env survives daemonization and ancestry does not; or (4) do not forward cmux hooks into sessions cmux hands off to Claude's bg daemon.

LOCAL WORKAROUND: none for a running session (--settings is read at launch; project settings.json merges, it cannot remove them). Editing the daemon's persisted respawnFlags (~/.claude/jobs/<id>/state.json, ~/.claude/daemon/roster.json) is NOT recommended -- the daemon rewrites state.json continuously and would clobber it.
close_reason: Fixed live via socketControlMode=automation; no restart needed. Sparkle auto-update staged separately.

comments.author: claude-conlang-fable
comments.text:
UPSTREAM STATUS (checked 2026-08-25): NOT FIXED. Do not update to fix this.

manaflow-ai/cmux issue #7100 — 'Claude Code Agents view detaches a live session from cmux's process tree -> all hooks rejected (Access denied), integration silently lost' — is our exact bug, verbatim same server reply. Filed 2026-06-30 against cmux 0.64.17, STILL OPEN as of today, i.e. open past the latest release v0.64.22 (2026-08-03). Related open: #1159 (ancestry check breaks after long uptime), #1864 (feature req: socket password auth).

Installed build here is 0.62.2 (77) commit 6c203b514 = 2026-03-14, ~5 months stale — but updating to 0.64.22 would NOT fix this.

WORKING KNOB (from #7100 comments, reporter verified end-to-end): set automation.socketControlMode = 'automation' (Settings > Automation; default is 'cmuxOnly'). The 'automation' mode allows local automation clients from this macOS user with NO ancestry check, and the daemon-hosted session still carries the right CMUX_SURFACE_ID so it reconnects and re-binds its surface. Env override CMUX_SOCKET_MODE=allowAll also exists. All 5 modes (off/cmuxOnly/automation/password/allowAll) are already present in the installed 0.62.2 binary, so no update is needed to use it.

TWO COSTS, both blocking a casual fix:
1. RESTART REQUIRED. Confirmed gotcha in #7100: changing socketControlMode does NOT take effect via 'cmux reload-config' — the stored value updates but the live listener keeps the old auth mode bound. The GUI/daemon process must be fully quit and relaunched.
2. SECURITY DOWNGRADE. It globally drops the ancestry boundary: any local process of this user can then drive the cmux control socket.

BLAST RADIUS of any cmux restart (measured on this machine): the cmux app (pid 1411, up since Jul 12) has 80 descendants, 68 of them shells/agents, and there is NO separate cmuxd daemon holding the PTYs — the app owns them via login processes. Quitting kills: 3 Claude sessions (pids 5564 'conlang' 17d, 46713 'roomtone' 27d, 69099 'roomtone-setup-automation' 27d) and ~10 Codex sessions aged 28-44 days.

RECOMMENDATION: do nothing now. The symptom is cosmetic (non-blocking, ~0.3s per prompt submit). Both remedies cost the same restart that wipes 13 long-running agent sessions. Bundle the socketControlMode change together with the 0.62.2 -> 0.64.x update the next time a cmux restart is acceptable anyway.

comments.text:
RESOLVED 2026-08-26 — live, with NO restart. Upstream's 'restart required' gotcha does NOT apply to 0.62.2.

ACTION: defaults write com.cmuxterm.app socketControlMode -string automation
(Verified against the source AT the installed commit 6c203b514: SocketControlSettings.appStorageKey = 'socketControlMode', plain UserDefaults in com.cmuxterm.app; defaultMode = .cmuxOnly, which is why the key was absent and we were denied; parseMode('automation') -> .automation; effectiveMode reads it with an optional CMUX_SOCKET_MODE env override. ~/.config/cmux/cmux.json does NOT exist on this build — that file store is a newer feature, so the legacy defaults key is the right lever here.)

RESULT — took effect IMMEDIATELY on the live listener, no quit/relaunch:
  cmux claude-hook prompt-submit  -> 'OK', exit 0   (was: 'Failed to write to socket', exit 1)
  cmux read-screen --surface ...  -> works          (was: same error)
  raw socket                      -> no 'Access denied' greeting
cmux app pid 1411 untouched (45d uptime preserved), all descendants intact.

This CONTRADICTS the #7100 comment claiming socketControlMode changes require a full app quit (reporter was on 0.64.17). On 0.62.2 the ACL mode is consulted per-connection. Worth adding to #7100 as a version-specific data point.

SECURITY NOTE: 'automation' drops the process-ancestry gate for local clients of this macOS user — any local process running as edward can now drive the cmux control socket. This is the mode cmux documents for exactly this purpose ('Automation tools (e.g. hooks for Claude, Cursor, Gemini) may connect'). Revert with:
  defaults delete com.cmuxterm.app socketControlMode     (back to cmuxOnly default)

SEPARATE: cmux was never checking for updates — SUEnableAutomaticChecks=0, SUAutomaticallyUpdate=0, SULastCheckTime=2026-05-02. That is why the install sat 5 months stale at 0.62.2 (2026-03-14) vs latest 0.64.22 (2026-08-03). The May Sparkle failure ('Failed to create installation cache directory') was transient; that dir now exists and is writable. Enabled background check + install-on-quit:
  defaults write com.cmuxterm.app SUEnableAutomaticChecks -bool true
  defaults write com.cmuxterm.app SUAutomaticallyUpdate -bool true
Sparkle will download in the background and install when cmux next quits — new version on next start, no forced relaunch. Deliberately did NOT hand-swap /Applications/cmux.app: live sessions reference CMUX_SHELL_INTEGRATION_DIR and Contents/Resources/bin/claude inside that bundle, and a code-signature mismatch on lazily-loaded frameworks could crash the running app — the exact 80-process wipe we are avoiding.

TO RE-VERIFY AFTER THE NEXT cmux START: 0.64.x moved settings to ~/.config/cmux/cmux.json. Confirm the legacy socketControlMode key still applies (run 'cmux claude-hook prompt-submit' and expect OK); if hooks break again, set automation.socketControlMode in the new config file instead.
